source_name: Društvo novinarjev Slovenije — investigative-journalism tag feed
why_relevant: Journalists' association tag page that surfaces which sl outlets and reporters are doing investigative finance work — a pointer for expanding the media actor map and identifying beat reporters covering Banka Slovenije.

source_name: Večer — Gospodarstvo (Maribor-based national daily)
why_relevant: Third national daily with a business desk; adds non-Ljubljana perspective on bank branch closures, savings-bank/ hranilnica supervision and regional consultation responses. Hypothesised section URL — not verified.

source_name: Siol.net — Posel danes (Telekom Slovenije portal)
why_relevant: High-traffic free sl portal republishing STA business copy; useful open-access mirror for regulatory and payments announcements. Section URL inferred, not verified.

source_name: STA English service (english.sta.si)
why_relevant: English wire output of the national agency; lets en-only pipelines pick up the same regulatory/consultation timeline that sl subscribers get, at lower volume. Bridges the sl/en language requirement of this run.

source_name: Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenija — customer regulatory notices (bank-as-publisher)
why_relevant: Banks' own sl-language customer notices state concrete compliance dates and operational interpretations of EU rules (e.g. Uredba EU 2024/886 instant payments, VoP payee verification from 9 Oct 2025) earlier and more plainly than regulator texts. Verified example found.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Pritožbe uporabnikov finančnih storitev (consumer complaints unit)
why_relevant: Central-bank landing page for consumer complaints against banks, savings banks, payment institutions, e-money issuers, payment system operators, bureaux de change and credit intermediaries; states the legal basis (ZPlaSSIED, ZPotK-2, ZVPot-1, ZPPDFT-2, ZCKR, ZSJV) and the escalation path into out-of-court settlement. Defines the complaints funnel whose volume/topics precede supervisory tightening.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Prijava kršitev v bankah in drugih nadzorovanih subjektih (whistle/violation reporting)
why_relevant: Separate reporting channel (breach reports rather than individual complaints). The categories the regulator invites reports on signal current supervisory attention; changes to this page hint at emerging conduct-risk priorities.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Potrošniško kreditiranje (consumer credit supervision section)
why_relevant: Supervisory section devoted to consumer credit conduct; carries findings from thematic reviews and expectations toward banks. Consumer-credit conduct findings routinely migrate into binding measures and macroprudential restrictions.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Primerjava stroškov bančnih storitev za potrošnike (fee comparison publications)
why_relevant: Recurring (roughly annual/semi-annual) regulator publication comparing retail banking and payment-service fees; a consumer-protection transparency instrument and a direct read on pricing pressure and where the regulator wants visibility. Latest observed edition February 2026.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) – IRPS / Alternative Dispute Resolution body
why_relevant: The recognised out-of-court consumer dispute resolution provider (izvajalec IRPS) for banking services in Slovenia. The mediator (posrednik) issues opinions; annual case statistics and published opinions are the single richest weak-signal stream on where retail banking/payments conduct is failing.

source_name: ZBS – Mnenja IRPS (published mediator opinions, PDF series)
why_relevant: Actual anonymised opinions in consumer-vs-bank disputes (e.g. account debits, online fraud/abuse, loan repayment). Case-level detail on disputed practices — card fraud liability, unauthorised transactions, fees — months before any supervisory circular.

source_name: Zveza potrošnikov Slovenije (ZPS) – news / novice
why_relevant: The main Slovenian consumer association; publishes analyses of ADR outcomes against banks (e.g. 'Kako uspešni so bili lani potrošniki v izvensodnih sporih z bankami?', June 2025), lobbies during consultations, and names specific bank practices. Leading indicator of political/supervisory pressure.

source_name: ZPS – Nasveti in vodniki / odgovori na vprašanja potrošnikov (payments & bank Q&A)
why_relevant: Consumer-facing guidance on payment-service rights and casework answers (e.g. 'Spletna zloraba – z odgovorom banke nisem zadovoljen'). Reveals the actual complaint archetypes consumers bring — online payment fraud, refusal of refunds — i.e. the demand side of the dispute channel.

source_name: ZPS – 'Kam se obrniti, ko so kratene pravice potrošnikom' (map of supervisory bodies)
why_relevant: Consumer-NGO-authored directory of Slovenian supervisory and complaint-handling institutions — an efficient actor-map seed for snowballing further ADR/complaint bodies beyond banking.

source_name: Register izvajalcev izvensodnega reševanja potrošniških sporov (IRPS register) – OPSI open data
why_relevant: Official machine-readable register of all recognised ADR providers under ZIsRPS (Ur. l. RS 81/15). Enumerates every body that can hear consumer-vs-bank/payment disputes — the definitive actor list for this cell, and changes to it show new/deregistered ADR bodies.

source_name: Ministrstvo za gospodarstvo, turizem in šport – consumer protection sector / IRPS provider list
why_relevant: The ministry maintaining the IRPS register and drafting consumer legislation (ZVPot-1, ZPotK-2). Legacy list URL was on mgrt.gov.si; content has migrated to gov.si, so the exact deep link must be re-discovered rather than assumed.

source_name: CNVOS – consultation watch (Aktualno) for consumer legislation
why_relevant: NGO umbrella body that flags open public consultations (e.g. 'V javni razpravi je predlog Zakona o varstvu potrošnikov') and tracks whether consultation rules were respected. Useful redundancy layer over e-demokracija and a signal of civil-society mobilisation.

source_name: Obrtno-podjetniška zbornica Slovenije (OZS) – IRPS / consumer-law guidance
why_relevant: Trade-chamber explainers on ADR obligations and consumer-law drafts, written for obliged traders. Shows how the obligation is understood/implemented on the business side and flags draft amendments early.

source_name: AZN – Agencija za zavarovalni nadzor, consumer complaints & dispute-resolution pages
why_relevant: Insurance supervisor's consumer section: how to complain, which ADR bodies are competent, and links to complaint routes. Relevant to the 'both sectors' scope and to bancassurance disputes sold through bank channels.

source_name: European Commission FIN-NET – members in Slovenia
why_relevant: Authoritative EU-level enumeration of the Slovenian financial ADR bodies with scope, languages and contact details — an independent cross-check on the national IRPS register and a stable way to detect new/removed Slovenian ADR schemes.

source_name: Varuh človekovih pravic RS – annual reports (consumer/financial-services chapters)
why_relevant: The national Human Rights Ombudsman handles consumer-related grievances only vis-à-vis state bodies and holders of public authority, but its annual reports surface systemic issues (e.g. basic payment account access, financial exclusion, personality-rights/privacy in banking) and generate political follow-up.

source_name: ATVP – Vlagatelji (investor complaints portal)
why_relevant: Securities Market Agency's investor-facing site covering complaint handling for investment services; investment firms must report complaint counts and reasons to ATVP, and disputes can go to the ZDU-GIZ arbitration. Adjacent conduct channel that shares distribution networks with banks.

source_name: ZDU-GIZ – Arbitraža (arbitration of the fund-management companies association)
why_relevant: ADR/arbitration body for disputes between investors and fund management companies; named in providers' complaint rules as the escalation route. Completes the map of sector-specific financial ADR bodies alongside ZBS and SZZ.

source_name: Bank/PSP published complaint & ADR terms (Splošni pogoji za opravljanje plačilnih storitev za potrošnike)
why_relevant: Every Slovenian bank must publish, in its consumer payment-services T&Cs, the internal complaint procedure and the ADR body it recognises as competent. Comparing these across banks reveals which institutions accept ZBS IRPS, deadlines they commit to, and drift after regulatory changes.

source_name: Insurer complaint-procedure pages (pritožbeni postopki) – Generali, GRAWE, Wiz, Merkur
why_relevant: Mandatory published complaint routes on insurer sites, naming the internal body, AZN and the SZZ ADR bodies. Same diff logic as bank T&Cs; also relevant for insurtech/bancassurance distribution.

source_name: European Commission – Alternative dispute resolution for consumers (SI page) / e-justice national bodies list
why_relevant: EU-level pointer into national ADR frameworks and the non-judicial bodies list for Slovenia; useful to detect EU-driven changes (ADR Directive revision, ODR platform decommissioning) that will force Slovenian channel redesign.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Kariera v Banki Slovenije (supervisor's own job postings)
why_relevant: The supervisor staffing up a named function (DORA oversight, crypto/MiCA, AML inspections, instant payments) is the earliest observable signal that a supervisory programme is being stood up, typically 6-18 months ahead of published expectations.
